🌟 Scribe | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: A unified environment for scientists to write research papers, embed dynamic content from Python notebooks, and manage all related assets locally.
✨ Key Features: • Integrated LaTeX paper editing with Python notebooks and figures • Local compilation using Tectonic or TeX Live • CodeMirror 6 editor with LaTeX-specific features (completion, snippets, hover info) • Support for TikZ diagrams
📖 Summary: Scribe is a desktop LaTeX editor designed for scientists, integrating LaTeX papers with Python notebooks and figures into a single project. It allows for seamless compilation of documents on the user's machine using Tectonic or TeX Live, ensuring privacy and local control.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 OpenTV-Remote | Kotlin
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a free, open-source, and highly customizable smart TV remote control application for their Android and iPhone devices, enabling local network control of various smart TVs.
✨ Key Features: • Free and open-source (MIT License) • No subscription, ads, or account required • Automatic network discovery
📖 Summary: OpenTV-Remote is a free, open-source mobile application for Android and iPhone that functions as a smart TV remote. It offers custom layouts, local Wi-Fi control, and supports English and Russian languages, with a focus on providing a seamless and user-friendly remote experience without requiring subscriptions or accounts.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ codeburn | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide developers with clear visibility and control over their AI coding tool token consumption and associated costs.
✨ Key Features: • Tracks AI coding token usage and cost • Supports 37 AI tools and agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini) • Provides breakdowns by model, project, and task • Offers both a CLI and a menubar/web dashboard interface • Local and free to use
📖 Summary: CodeBurn is a free, local tool designed to track AI coding token usage and associated costs across numerous AI tools and agents. It provides detailed breakdowns by model, project, and task, offering visibility into AI spending.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 open-source-games | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Discovering and accessing open-source video games and their source code.
✨ Key Features: • Curated list of open-source games • Categorization by genre • Links to game websites • Links to source code repositories • Includes remakes of commercial games
📖 Summary: This repository is a curated list of open-source video games and open-source remakes of commercial games. It categorizes these games by genre, providing links to their respective websites and source code repositories.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 OpenGait | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Developing, training, and evaluating custom gait recognition models.
✨ Key Features: • Flexible and extensible framework • Gait recognition model design and comparison • Support for multiple datasets (GaitLU-1M, SUSTech1K, etc.) • Integration of advanced models (FoundationGait, BiggerGait, DenoisingGait, etc.) • Published research in top-tier conferences (CVPR, TPAMI, ECCV, NeurIPS, MICCAI, AAAI)
📖 Summary: OpenGait is a flexible and extensible Python framework for gait recognition, enabling researchers to design and compare state-of-the-art models. It supports various datasets and has been highlighted in CVPR2023 and TPAMI2025.
